purpose.turn_behavioral_observations_int: A data engineering portfolio project. A Python, Databricks and dbt pipeline collects player records over time and turns them into audiences you can compare. Simulated purchases demonstrate the customer-analysis step.
purpose.league_of_legends_is_an_online_g: League of Legends is an online game where people choose characters and can play competitive matches. This project uses that game's records as a case study in understanding user behavior. You do not need to know the game to follow along.
purpose.riot_s_api_supplies_dated_charac: Riot's API supplies dated records of character use and competitive play. These records are the source of the profiles.
purpose.models_turn_those_records_into_e: Models turn those records into estimates and audience descriptions. They help us compare groups; they do not explain why people behave differently.
purpose.generated_purchase_records_demon: These purchases demonstrate commercial analysis on real profiles, but they do not show what players actually bought.
purpose.introduce_activity_and_competiti: See activity and competitive standing, one dimension at a time.
purpose.explore_character_interests_then: See character preferences, then combine these characteristics to define an audience.
purpose.carry_that_audience_into_the_sim: Compare that audience's simulated purchases and see the engineering behind the analysis.
purpose.compact_repeated_observations_bu: Compact records collected over time describe users with few API requests. Each chapter opens with an overview, and the question menu opens the comparisons. In Combine, you define an audience and can carry it into Purchases.
purpose.byline: Built by Pedro Iaki · solo project · behavioral data from Riot's API · simulated purchases
purpose.how_the_evidence_reaches_this_st: From collected data to this dashboard
purpose.collection_dated_history_and_aud: Collection and modeling produce the local data behind this dashboard. Simulated purchases add an example of a commercial integration. Select a step to open its code or documentation.

interest.every_member_clears_15k_in_this: Every member clears 15k in this example. Full active lifetime mastery is the denominator. Spread reflects overlapping scores, not six independent interests.
stages.the_file_reached_the_landing_volu: The file reached the landing volume. Ingestion is not confirmed; delivery-related freshness and normal cleanup must wait.
stages.raw_observations_were_delivered_r: Raw observations were delivered. Registry and local ledger updates are separate service boundaries; a later failure does not undo confirmed ingestion.

stages.the_viewer_reads_the_checked_loca: The dashboard reads the checked local files without data warehouse credentials. A successful model run does not refresh them automatically.
chapter.primer.accumulated_play_competit: Accumulated play, competitive frequency and recorded history describe different sides of activity. Competitive games are only one way to play. History shows how long activity has been visible, not when the account was created.
chapter.primer.standing_is_a_position_on: Standing places each player on a competitive ladder. The reference shows how common each band is. Explore how activity and standing relate, or compare standing within one frequency band.
chapter.primer.characters_have_different: Character choices point to patterns of interest. Characters that share audiences form families that can overlap, and eight archetypes summarize how players combine those families. One person can show several archetypes. The names describe play preferences, not skill or commercial value.
chapter.primer.construct_an_audience_by_: Combine the characteristics from earlier chapters. Set the filters shared by both audiences, choose the conditions for A and B, and check how many people are in each audience and in both.
chapter.primer.these_audiences_are_linke: The same audiences are now linked to simulated purchases. Compare how many people buy, how much they spend, how often they buy and whether they favor cosmetic items or new characters.
comparison.how_do_these_constructed_audi: What differs between the audiences you defined?
comparison.a_and_b_describe_the_same_sel: A and B describe the same selected audience. Change the conditions to compare different groups.
comparison.shared_conditions_describe_gr: Shared filters define the groups; they do not make people equivalent in every other way. To compare interests, the reference uses the profiles the model scored within those filters.
questions.controls.only_the_comparison_d: These controls adjust the compared characteristic; shared filters stay fixed.
charts.median.weighted_median_within_the: Weighted median of the profiles in this band. Not everyone has this value.
charts.distribution.limited_support_requ: Not enough data: needs at least 30 profiles and an effective sample size of 20.
charts.heatmap.share_of_the_original_beh: Share of the full behavioral base · fixed 0–10% color scale.
charts.heatmap.joint_share_within_this_a: Share of this audience in each combination · fixed 0–100% color scale.
charts.heatmap.categories_stay_fixed_acr: {value} Bands stay the same when you select another audience. Cells marked “limited” have few profiles but stay in the calculation; check a cell to see how many it holds.
scale.primary_interest_over_under_the_pa: Primary interest: above or below the reference
scale.original_weights_denominator_score: Keeps the original weights. Percentages use every profile the model scored, including those with no clear match or with ties.
charts.median.limited_scored_support_con: Few profiles scored by the model. The chosen filters were kept.
charts.median.selected_primary_share_par: Primary-interest share in the audience ÷ share in the reference − 1. Zero means the same share; +50% means 1.5 times the reference share. If the reference is zero, the comparison is unavailable. This does not correct for character popularity.
charts.distribution.interest_over_under_: Interests relative to the reference · set by your filters
charts.distribution.identical_audiences_: A and B are the same. You can still compare this audience's interests with the reference.
charts.distribution.primary_identity_is_: Your filters already restrict the primary interest, so its share here follows from the selection. It is not a finding.
interests.companions.full_selected_audie: Percentages use the whole selected audience. The model needs at least four active characters to score a profile. A profile without a score is not a profile without interests.
interests.limited_scored_support: Few profiles scored by the model.
interests.no_additional_archetype_meets_: No other archetype reaches the minimum strength to appear here. Smaller affinities may still exist.
interests.companions.limited_scored_supp: Few profiles scored by the model.
interests.companions.this_side_contains_: This group includes profiles with several expressed interests.
interests.companions.single_and_blend_pr: The base keeps profiles with one or several expressed interests.
interests.companions.share_of_selected_s: Share of this audience's scored profiles with strength ≥0.20 in each archetype. {value} One person can appear in several; the shares are not a corrected popularity ranking.
interestOnly.observed_profiles_of_the_ad: {profiles} observed profiles · {value} of the adjusted base · effective N {effective_n}
why.a_customer_can_have_substantial_hist: A customer can have used a product heavily over the years and rarely visit it today. Volume, frequency and history describe different things. Here, competitive games cover only one way of using the product.
why.audience_composition_can_change_a_po: Differences in audience composition can change a comparison's result. Here, standing gives context for the groups; it does not indicate a customer's worth.
why.in_retail_products_repeatedly_chosen: In retail, products repeatedly chosen by the same customers can form product groups, and customers’ mixes across them can describe interests. Here the observations are character usage, not shopping baskets or all market sales.
why.intersect_characteristics_to_define_: Cross characteristics to define an audience for a product question, then check whether enough people remain to describe it.
why.buyer_participation_spending_per_buy: Knowing how many people buy, how much each buyer spends and which items they get answers different product questions.
comparison.read_accumulated_play_and_com: Relate accumulated play and competitive participation
comparison.distribution_within_this_stan: Distribution within this standing band. Small groups stay included.
interests.adcs_ranged_sustained_attacker: ADCs: ranged sustained attackers (attack damage carries).
interests.primary_match_selects_a_unique: Primary: the single strongest archetype, with no tie, at strength 0.20 or higher. Expressed: any chosen archetype that reaches 0.20. Choosing several matches players who fit any one of them.

builder.select_any_number_of_segments_no: Choose one or more bands. With no selection, the field does not restrict the audience, even where the value is unavailable. Collapsing a section keeps its filters active.

builder.results_reflect_the_applied_defi: The charts show the applied filters.

metric.how_much_per_purchaser: How much does each buyer spend?
metric.limited_member_support: Too few profiles in this scenario.
metric.repeat_share_among_purchasers: Buyers with two or more purchases
metric.scenario_members_cash_purchasers: {value} profiles in the scenario · {value2} bought with cash
metric.participation_includes_nonbuyers_: The buyer rate also counts people who did not buy. Spending per buyer is in US dollars over the scenario's 60 days. Cosmetic items change appearance; unlocks add playable characters. The cosmetic share covers all cosmetic and character acquisitions across the simulated history and counts acquisitions, not amounts spent.
simulation.how_this_purchase_scenario_wa: How this purchase scenario was built
simulation.the_scenario_combines_real_be: The scenario combines real behavioral profiles with explicitly designed spending assumptions and reproducible random variation. These shape purchase frequency, transaction activity and content choices so the complete customer-reporting workflow can be demonstrated and verified.
simulation.the_specialist_modifier_adds_: For profiles classified as specialists, the generator adds 0.10 to the setting that favors cosmetic items. Other adjustments, limits and random draws also apply, so this does not guarantee a 10-point difference in the final chart.
simulation.generated_events_survive_iden: Events pass through profile linking, dated modeling and reconciliation. Finding a generator-imposed relationship in the report shows this path preserved it. It does not validate that relationship for real customers.
simulation.cash_top_ups_count_as_cash_on: Cash top-ups count as cash once. Spending game currency on content is a separate event, not more cash revenue. The eight archetypes were attached later, not used as generator inputs.
f.saved_pair_co_assignment_0_100_color_s: How often each pair landed in the same group · 0–100% color scale
families.evidence.all_173_characters_are: All 173 characters are covered in 25 overlapping families, with 251 memberships. Minimum family consistency is 94%. The accepted relative-Jaccard floor balances coverage, fit and family count.
families.evidence.the_review_floor_compa: The review floor compares a character's audience relationship with its own alternative-family reference. Stricter settings do not monotonically improve every measure. Twenty-four selected families use 20-repeat sources; one uses a 100-repeat source.
families.evidence.inspect_a_frozen_compo: Explore an archetype from the adopted model
families.evidence.nmf_learned_eight_nonn: NMF learned eight nonnegative family profiles. Players can express mixtures; inference applies the same frozen profiles and training weights without refitting.
families.evidence.strongest_six_family_c: Strongest six family coordinates in the accepted unweighted-affinity profile scale; bars relative to this component's largest coordinate. These are strengths, not probabilities. No archetype-bootstrap stability is asserted. Names received informal player feedback.
families.evidence.the_toy_uses_cutoff_qu: This example requires a minimum mastery score per character to calculate affinities. The archetype model uses a different rule: all active characters, weighted by lifetime mastery, with no such cutoff.
families.evidence.weighted_audience_rela: Weighted audience relationships and strongest-neighbor graphs supported Leiden discovery. Full and anchored searches supplied candidates. Resampling and reviewed coverage/member-fit gates shaped the final overlapping families; this is not one automatic partition.
families.evidence.characters_repeatedly_: Characters repeatedly grouped together when source players were resampled. Overlap is intentional: {value} members also occur in another accepted family.
families.evidence.fit_of_each_member_rev: Fit of each member · review floor 80%
families.evidence.self_pairs_excluded_we: Self-pairs excluded. Weakest member: {value}. These saved diagnostics were reused in selection; they are not held-out accuracy or calibrated confidence. Matrix and fit come from this family's exact saved source, not pooled sources.
families.evidence.accepted_family_eviden: Adopted family evidence and selection limits
capabilities.full_page_discovery_uses_20: Full-page discovery uses 206 core calls for 205 players; ordinary known-player refresh uses two.
capabilities.at_discovery_and_follow_up_: At discovery and follow-up. Repeated compact observations trade match detail for broader history. These are conditional costs, not measured throughput.
capabilities.partial_work_needs_an_expla: Partial work needs an explanation before retry or cleanup.
capabilities.sqlite_links_source_tasks_t: SQLite links source tasks to files, compaction and load state.
capabilities.at_integrity_gates_and_diag: At integrity gates and diagnosis. This is task/file lineage, not automated column lineage.
capabilities.reapplying_a_dated_observat: Reapplying a dated observation must not reapply its refresh effects.
capabilities.postgresql_upserts_require_: PostgreSQL upserts require a newer observation timestamp; repeated/older observations are ignored.
capabilities.after_confirmed_ingestion_a: After confirmed ingestion and during state-update retries. This scoped idempotency does not imply end-to-end exactly-once delivery.
capabilities.competing_claimants_need_di: Competing claimants need distinct work and recoverable ownership.
capabilities.postgresql_row_locks_skip_l: PostgreSQL row locks, SKIP LOCKED and claim tokens reserve work; expiry and renewal handle stale owners.
capabilities.during_discovery_and_refres: During discovery and refresh. Atomicity is within the database transaction; a multi-machine deployment has not been demonstrated.
capabilities.concurrent_calls_can_otherw: Concurrent calls can otherwise overspend a shared client allowance.
capabilities.locks_and_a_token_bucket_co: Locks and a token bucket coordinate requests within one client.
capabilities.during_api_calls_shared_cla: During API calls. Shared claims do not globally throttle separate clients. Current evidence does not establish an actively multithreaded production runner.
capabilities.an_upload_can_succeed_while: An upload can succeed while ingestion or modeling fails.
capabilities.wait_for_confirmed_ingestio: Wait for confirmed ingestion before dependent completion updates; run dbt separately and preserve inputs if a later stage fails.
capabilities.at_every_delivery_cycle_ser: At every delivery cycle. Service boundaries are not one distributed transaction; injected live recovery remains untested.
capabilities.stage_outcomes_must_explain: Stage outcomes must explain both success and partial work.
capabilities.console_events_job_results_: Console events, job results, integrity reports and the ledger retain different parts of the execution story.
capabilities.during_operation_and_review: During operation and review. Fixed report paths can be overwritten; archive matching records by run.
capabilities.reviewers_need_a_usable_res: Reviewers need a usable result without warehouse credentials.
capabilities.versioned_models_an_explici: Versioned models, an explicit manifest and checked local Parquet files feed the dashboard.
capabilities.at_export_and_viewing_refre: At export and viewing. Refresh is manual and snapshot dates remain visible.

render.three_dimensions_of_activity_thre: Three dimensions of activity. Three different questions.
render.how_much_accumulated_play_how_oft: How much have people played, how often do they compete, and how far back does their recorded activity go?
render.estimated_hours_lifetime_mastery_: Estimated hours = lifetime mastery points / 1,200, assuming 600 points and 30 minutes per match. Frequency is recorded competitive wins + losses under a one-year-season assumption. History is a minimum known span from retained last-play timestamps. Terminology changes labels, not membership.
render.next_competitive_standing_adds_po: Next: beyond how much people play, see where they sit on the competitive ladder.
render.compare_positions_on_the_ladder_w: See how ladder position relates to the activity dimensions.
render.next_character_choices_add_intere: Next: character choices point to interests.
render.which_interest_patterns_accompany: Which interest patterns accompany different behavioral profiles?
render.understand_the_archetype_names_an: Understand the archetype names and mixtures
render.adcs_means_ranged_sustained_attac: ADCs means ranged sustained attackers (attack damage carries). Bruisers/Tanks are durable close-range characters; Mages/Enchanters use spells or strengthen allies; Assassins/Duelists favor focused attacks; Front-Line Disablers interrupt; Control Mages restrict space; Burst Mages concentrate damage; Aggressive Junglers initiate pressure from between lanes.
render.single_one_strength_meets_0_20_bl: Single: one strength meets 0.20. Blend: several meet it. Diffuse: none does. A primary interest is set only when one strength is highest with no tie and meets 0.20; naming feedback is not statistical validation.
render.choose_a_question_above_primary_i: Choose a question above. Primary-interest comparisons include every profile with a clear primary interest, with no activity filters applied beforehand.
render.construct_an_audience_around_your: Define the audience for your question.
render.edit_the_shared_context_and_indep: Choose the shared filters and the conditions for A and B, then apply the comparison.
render.intersection_profiles_of_original: In both audiences: {profiles} profiles · {value} of the full adjusted base · {customers} profiles in the purchase scenario. A and B can share people.
render.next_opens_purchases_using_the_la: The next chapter uses the last applied filters to compare purchases. Unapplied changes are left out.
render.connect_audiences_to_customer_que: How do these audiences buy in the simulated scenario?
render.the_same_audience_predicates_sele: The same filters select the matching people in the simulated purchase data. Here every person counts equally, with no population weighting.
